brief.summary: Iqbal Day, observed every November 9, marks the birthday of Allama Muhammad Iqbal (born 1877, Sialkot) — poet, philosopher, and widely regarded as the ideological founder of Pakistan. At the 1930 Allahabad Address he was the first to articulate the two-nation theory that led to Pakistan's creation in 1947.
key_messages: Iqbal is remembered as the 'Poet of the East' for his Urdu and Persian poetry.
His philosophy of Khudi (selfhood) and the symbol of the Shaheen (eagle) continue to inspire national pride and resilience, especially among youth.
Iqbal Day was reinstated as an official public holiday in 2022 after being discontinued in 2015.
dos: Frame Iqbal as an inspirational, unifying figure for students and educators.
Reference Khudi/Shaheen to connect with a youth audience.
donts: Do not wade into modern partisan debates about Iqbal's legacy.
Do not fabricate quotes or verses without a verifiable source.
Avoid dry/academic language given the brand's warm tone.
unverified_claims: 'Ideological founder'/'spiritual father of Pakistan' is a widely repeated characterization, not a formal title — flagged as reputation, not fact.

concepts.core_message: Every child carries a spark of Khudi (selfhood) — the belief that you can become who you're meant to be
concepts.visual_direction: A child looking up toward a bright sky/horizon, soft warm-glow lighting

copy.one_liner: Every child carries a spark of Khudi.
copy.caption: Allama Iqbal believed each of us holds the power to become who we're meant to be. This Iqbal Day, remind the next generation that their own spark of self-belief is worth nurturing.
copy.cta: Nurture the spark in your child today.

visual.layout_instructions: Portrait poster; child silhouette bottom third looking toward a bright horizon; headline across the clear upper two-thirds; logo bottom-right, clear space = logo height ÷ 2
visual.image_prompt: Warm, soft-lit illustration of a young child looking upward toward a bright horizon, warm orange-to-cream gradient background, rounded soft shapes, child-friendly and hopeful mood, no rendered text, negative space reserved at top
visual.composition_notes: Keep top two-thirds clear for headline overlay; soft shadows only, no hard edges

concepts.core_message: Meet the poet who first dreamed of Pakistan, 17 years before it existed
concepts.visual_direction: A timeline/quill-and-book motif referencing 1930 Allahabad Address to 1947

copy.one_liner: Meet the poet who dreamed of Pakistan.
copy.caption: In 1930, seventeen years before Pakistan existed, Allama Iqbal was the first to give voice to the idea in his historic Allahabad Address. Born in Sialkot in 1877, he became known across the world as the 'Poet of the East.'
copy.cta: Share his story with a student today.

visual.composition_notes: Keep timeline strip and headline area clear of illustration detail

concepts.core_message: Aim high. Fly like the Shaheen.
concepts.visual_direction: Minimal eagle silhouette, high contrast, negative space

copy.caption: Iqbal's eagle — the Shaheen — never settles for less than the sky.
